note: What Brew can have made, one entry per asset. Families (family: null) are the make.format values cards use and keep every old name so saved packs still map; Sloosh Spaces and models carry family: the format they produce. [product] in an example is replaced by the brand's own product name when the block is rendered. Brand-agnostic.

formats.looks: One still frame for Meta or Google: the product in a scene or on a clean ground with a headline, made as 3 to 6 hook versions.
formats.with: Brew statics (Chromium lettering) or Sloosh Product Poster / Ad Creative
examples: 4:5 static: [product] on the pillow at 6 am, headline in the top third, price line under it
3 hooks, 1:1: [product] held up to the window light, each headline a different review line
4:5 static: [product] next to the rival's size on a kitchen scale, one line on the difference

formats.looks: A paid Meta carousel of 3 to 6 cards, each card one product, one proof or one step, swiping to a buy card.
formats.with: Brew carousels or Sloosh 3x3 Product Ad Grid
examples: 5 cards: [product] on five body types, same pose, same light, size named on each card
4 cards: the ingredient, the lab line, the 30-day result quote, the price
6 cards: one card per colourway of [product], the shade name as the only text

formats.looks: A Meta collection ad: one hero image or 8 s clip on top and four catalog products under it, opening full screen.
formats.with: Brew statics for the hero, Meta catalog for the grid
examples: Hero: [product] mid-use on the sofa, 4 catalog tiles: the three kits and the refill
Hero 8 s clip: the box opening on the doormat, grid: the four best sellers under 2,000
Hero: the winter shelf at home, grid: the four products the reviews name most

formats.looks: Dynamic product ads from the connected catalog: a frame or overlay design applied to every product card.
examples: One frame: the price tag in the brand colour on the bottom left, free-shipping line on the top edge
Two frames to test: review stars under the product vs the 30-day promise under the product
Retargeting frame: 'still in your cart' in the brand font over the product card
formats.short: one frame over every catalog card

formats.looks: A paid 9:16 or 1:1 clip, 6 to 30 s, with timed beats, captions and an end card; made from product photos, not a shoot.
formats.with: Seedance 2.5 (timed beats), Kling V3 Omni, Veo 3.1, or Sloosh Cinematic Ad Sequence / UGC Selfie Video Ad
examples: 9:16, 12 s: 0-3 s [product] heating up on a desk, 3-8 s the hand sliding in, 8-12 s the price and the 30-day line
9:16 selfie, 15 s: a buyer reads her own review line to camera holding [product], caption burned in
1:1, 8 s: [product] in the rival's box size then ours, one line on the difference, end card
formats.short: paid clip with timed beats and end card

formats.looks: One organic feed image for the brand's own account, in its own photo style, with a caption written natively.
formats.with: Brew statics or Sloosh Product in Scene + Relight
examples: 4:5 post: [product] on the window ledge at golden hour, caption the founder's one-line origin story
1:1 post: [product] relit on a dark ground, caption a question to the audience about their routine
4:5 post: the ingredient and [product] side by side, caption the lab line from the site
formats.short: one organic feed image and caption

formats.looks: An organic swipe of 4 to 8 slides on the brand's own account: a how-to, a comparison, a review set or a lookbook.
formats.with: Brew carousels or Sloosh Instagram Carousel
examples: 6 slides: the fit room, one body type per slide, size named on each
5 slides: the five questions buyers ask most, one answer per slide, [product] on the last
7 slides: a week of mornings with [product], one day per slide, the routine as the caption

formats.looks: A set of 3 to 5 vertical frames for Stories: a poll, a swipe-up to a page, a countdown or a behind-the-scenes set.
formats.with: Brew statics (9:16) or Sloosh Design Recomposer for the resize
examples: 4 frames: [product] in the box, in the hand, in use, the link frame with the price
3 frames: a poll on which shade of [product] to restock first, the answer frame the next day
5 frames: the packing table on a Friday, one order per frame, the last frame the review count

formats.looks: An organic 9:16 clip of 5 to 20 s for Reels, Shorts or TikTok, built on a 4-beat grid with captions and sound.
formats.with: Brew reels (Veo) or Sloosh Multishot Product Clips / UGC Unboxing Clip
examples: 9:16 reel, 8 s: [product] heating up on a desk, then the hand sliding in
9:16 reel, 12 s: unboxing [product] on the doormat, the card inside read out loud
9:16 reel, 15 s: three ways to wear [product] cut on the beat, the size on screen each time

formats.looks: One WhatsApp or SMS message with a product image, under 300 characters, sent to one segment at one moment.
examples: 1 message to buyers of [product] 30 days in: the refill with its price and the reorder link
1 message to cart leavers after 2 hours: the product left behind, the free-shipping line, the cart link
1 message to the last 90 days' buyers: the restock of [product] in the shade they bought
formats.short: one message with a product image, one segment

formats.looks: One email or a flow of 2 to 4 emails: subject line, hero image, 60 to 120 words, one button.
examples: 3-email welcome flow: the founder's line, the three best sellers with prices, the first-order code
1 email to [product] buyers at day 45: the review ask with the one-click stars
2-email win-back: 'what changed since you left' with the new [product], then the last-chance code
formats.short: one email or a 2-4 email flow

formats.looks: One section on a store page: a review strip, a comparison table, a size guide, an FAQ block or a hero, written for the theme.
formats.with: Brew page sections or Sloosh Collection Banner
examples: Review strip under add to cart on the [product] page: 3 quotes, the total count, the stars
Comparison table on the [product] page: us vs the two rivals the reviews name, 5 rows
Size guide above add to cart: the fit room photos per size, the measure-at-home steps
formats.short: one section on a store page

formats.looks: An asset none of the families cover: name it exactly in pieces (what, how many, which product, where it runs).
examples: Amazon listing pack for [product]: 7 gallery images, the A+ module, the title
Packaging mock of the new [product] box from the dieline, front and side
360 orbit of [product] for the product page, 24 frames
